title: Capacity scouting brief — 2027-02-10
content:
Capacity Scouting Brief — Feb 10 2027
Ownership: Ava Martinez (infra lead)
Quick summary:
- Purpose: weekly scout of fleet capacity signals, small prewarm experiment readouts, and regional surge preparations for Q1-Surge sim (planned 2027-03-08).
- Top-line: Utilization ticked up ~4% week-over-week; two short multi-hour preemptions in eu-west caused failover to us-west with minor latency impact. Prewarm experiment (short KV priming) reduced cold-start error rates but needs tuning to avoid cost regression on long-tail requests.
Attendees:
- Ava Martinez, Samir Patel, Lina Huang, Diego Rios, Priya Nair, Faye Okoro (SRE)
Observed metrics (last 7 days):
- Avg GPU utilization (cluster): 67% (up from 63% last week)
- P95 latency (generation): 210ms overall; eu-west P95 spiked to 380ms during preemptions
- Cold-start rate (on-demand models): 4.8% -> 1.8% with short prewarm (see experiment below)
- Preferential preemption window (cloud provider): 02:00-05:00 UTC for eu-west (observed)
Per-region notes:
- us-west-2: steady growth from marketing batch jobs; recommendation: cap burst capacity to preserve Dedicated pool SLA. File ticket JIRA-OPS-1187 to adjust burst policy.
- eu-west-1: observed 2 planned preemptions that caused autoscaler thrash for ~18m; mitigation: increase scale-down delay by +90s for TILted pools. Samir to iterate on policy.
- apac-sg: low baseline but high variance; still recommended to keep a small hot-pool (3 gpus) for low-latency customers in region.
Prewarm experiment (short-KV priming) — notes:
- Hypothesis: a brief automated prefix+KV prime on model hot-paths reduces cold-start error rate and P95 for first requests without large cost overhead.
- Setup: target models: /gptx-s-6b, /fastchat-13b; prime size: 8 tokens average per model; prewarm TTL 120s after idle; trigger threshold: idle > 30s
- Results (A/B over 72h): cold-start error down 62%, median first-request latency down 45ms, cost delta +6% total GPU-billing across test pool (due to extra short-lived kernels).
- Observations: cost impact concentrated on long-tail models that are rarely used; prime TTL of 120s seems too aggressive for infrequent models.
- Decision: continue but narrow scope to top-10 traffic models and reduce TTL to 30s. Lina to push config change and run 7-day follow-up.
Failure and incident notes:
- Incident: partial failover eu-west (2027-02-08 02:34 UTC) caused by maintenance preemption; autoscaler responded but some requests routed to us-west experienced 12% higher token cost due to model variant fallback. Root cause: provider maintenance + our fallback policy selection which favored larger model variants under capacity stress.
- Short-term mitigation taken: manual capacity handoff, temporary routing cap on variant promotion.
- Long-term action: implement capacity-weighted fallback policy (next-gen routing). Diego owning prototype (JIRA-OPS-1123).
Action items (owner — due):
- Reduce prewarm TTL to 30s and scope to top-10 models (Lina Huang — 2027-02-14)
- Adjust eu-west scale-down delay +90s on TILted pools (Samir Patel — 2027-02-12)
- Prototype capacity-weighted fallback routing (Diego Rios — draft by 2027-02-21; link: JIRA-OPS-1123)
- Add burst-cap flag to us-west Dedicated pools to limit marketing batch spillover (Ava Martinez — 2027-02-16; link: JIRA-OPS-1187)
- Run Q1-surge sim (full cross-region surge test) plan and dry-run checklist (Priya Nair — 2027-02-24)
Open questions / items for leadership:
- Acceptable cost delta for broad prewarm vs. user-perceived latency improvements? Current test shows +6% cost for ~45ms first-request improvement; leadership to advise if we should trade cost for latency for top-traffic models.
- Reserve budget for emergency burst capacity in APAC for upcoming partner launch (decision needed by 2027-02-18).
Notes to self / informal thoughts:
- Consider dynamic TTL that decays with model coldness score instead of fixed TTLs.
- Could combine prewarm with light quantized warm copies for ultra-rare but costly-large-model fallbacks.
- Add a lightweight telemetry tag on primed kernels to attribute cost precisely (helps show ROI).
Meeting adjourned — next sync: 2027-02-17 09:00 UTC (ops sync).
